scenes.say: Season finale, two drivers level on points. How did one lap decide the title?
Both on three sixty-nine and a half. The first time since nineteen seventy-four.
Verstappen starts from pole, but Hamilton passes him at the start.
Max attacks into Turn six. Hamilton cuts the chicane, stays ahead. No investigation.
Hamilton pulls away. By lap fifty-one he is over eleven seconds clear.
Lap fifty-three. Latifi crashes, and the safety car comes out.
Verstappen gets fresh softs. Hamilton stays out on old tyres to keep the lead.
Five lapped cars sit between the leaders. First message: they may not overtake.
Lap fifty-seven. Masi changes the decision: only those five may overtake.
Three stay put. Verstappen starts the last lap right behind Hamilton.
He passes Hamilton at Turn five, holds on to the flag and becomes champion.
Mercedes' protests rejected, appeal withdrawn. In February the FIA removed Masi.
The FIA report: human error, results final. Now all lapped cars are let past.
But one race doesn't decide a title. Before Abu Dhabi, both sides lost points.
Silverstone: a collision, a fifty-one g impact. Hamilton wins despite a penalty.
Hungary: a wet-start pile-up. Verstappen two points, Hamilton eighteen.
Baku: Verstappen's tyre fails, Hamilton goes off at the restart. Zero for both.
Monza: Verstappen is found responsible. The cars tangle, and both retire.
Jeddah: a penalty for Verstappen's erratic braking. Hamilton wins, they're level.
In the end, eight points over twenty-two races. A title is built over the whole season.

title: Abu Dhabi 2021: how F1's most controversial title was decided, and why it wasn't decided by one race
